purpose: One ordered ladder per job so an agent picks the cheapest live engine and stops. Read by _os/automation/bin/browser-access.js. Engines marked agent_tool cannot be driven from a CLI - only an agent holding that tool can call them, and the CLI reports them so the ladder stays honest rather than looking shorter than it is.

forbidden.why: Port 9222 and the default profile carry Dillon's live logged-in sessions. Driving them from an agent turns a read into an authenticated action against a client account.

webfetch.note: Cheapest. Static, known URL. No JS.

firecrawl_search.note: Searches and scrapes in one call. ~5 credits per query.

firecrawl_scrape.note: One URL to markdown. No proxy option on this schema.

firecrawl_batch_stealth.note: The ONLY Firecrawl schema exposing proxy:stealth. Use for Cloudflare and bot detection. SEARCH and SCRAPE have no proxy field.

direct_http.note: Plain HTTPS GET from Node. The CLI stand-in for WebFetch on static pages.

playwright_mcp.note: Isolated sidecar. JS interaction and snapshots. An 'Extension connection timeout' means the WRONG server was used - Cursor's --extension Playwright is a different process and is refused.

chrome_isolated.note: Dedicated profile only. Verified 2026-08-18 running --user-data-dir=C:\Users\dillo\claude-chrome. Never the default profile, never 9222.

camofox.note: Volume stealth. Refused until /health answers. Clone with System/scripts/Clone-CamofoxBrowser.py; no npm install unless asked.

brightdata.note: Inert without the key. Skills are installed but will fail on first use.

claude_in_chrome.note: The only engine that can reach logged-in Ads, Gmail, or GBP. Runs on Dillon's desktop against his real sessions, so an agent may recommend it and never drive it unattended.

history_export.note: Owned history only. Destination is gitignored and must never be committed.
